newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Swiss judge ends Sri Lanka paedophile inquiry.
newsitem.headline: Swiss judge ends Sri Lanka paedophile inquiry.

text.p: A Swiss judge investigating the activities of a suspected Swiss paedophile in Sri Lanka said on Tuesday he has concluded the investigation and would be returning to Switzerland on Wednesday.

Judge Jacques de Lavallaz said he and his team of two Swiss police officers recorded statements from several people who had come in contact with Bernard Lamon, a suspected child abuser who was arrested in Switzerland last November.

Lamon, a part-time resident of Sri Lanka since 1983, was arrested with an unidentified Sri Lankan boy. He was charged with sexually abusing several Sri Lankan children and with trafficking in children for sexual purposes, he said.
The evidence collected would be used for the suspect's prosecution in Switzerland, where the maximum sentence for child sexual abuse is a five-year jail term, Lavallaz said.

Lavallaz is the first foreign judge to visit Sri Lanka to investigate alleged crimes commited here by a foreign national, Mohammed Nizam, deputy inspector-general of the police crimes, branch told the same news conference. "His visit will undoubtedly send a strong message to the world's paedophiles," Nizam said.
Sri Lanka has been cooperating with Swiss authorities in a bid to clamp down on child abusers operating in the country, widely believed to be a popular destination for the world's paedophiles.
Nizam said another team of investigators from Switzerland was expected in Sri Lanka soon, this time on the trail of victims of a suspected child abuser deported from the island last month.
Swiss authorities remanded 54-year-old Viktor Baumann after he was deported. A Zurich court is scheduled to try him for alleged child abuse in Sri Lanka.
Last week, a Sri Lankan court sentenced in absentia another Swiss suspect, Thomas Kaspar-wirz, to two years in prison on charges of child sex abuse.

In February, a Sri Lankan court sentenced 58-year-old Swiss national Armin Heinrich Pfaffhauser to two years in jail for child sexual abuse. Pfaffhauser was the first foreigner to be convicted of the offence. He had pleaded not guilty.
